repairs.description: White argues that Emmaus links the disciples’ recognition of Jesus to Scripture’s prophetic testimony, which becomes unintelligible if no prophecy genuinely anticipated him.
repairs.rationale: This preserves White’s connection between recognition, prophetic testimony, and the implied problem for a reading without genuine prediction while forming a complete sentence.

repairs.description: Crossan argues that Markan priority makes Gospel agreement dependent rather than independently corroborative, while Matthew’s and Luke’s alterations expose their contextual theological aims.
repairs.rationale: This preserves Crossan’s two-part inference about reduced evidential independence and the interpretive significance of later Gospel alterations in one complete sentence.
